newsitem.title: UK: London platinum, palladium fix at fresh lows.
newsitem.headline: London platinum, palladium fix at fresh lows.

text.p: Platinum fixed at $377.75 an ounce on Wednesday morning, the lowest fixing since December 8, 1993, amid bearish market sentiment across the precious metals complex.
Its sister metal palladium was also set lower, fixing at $114.75 an ounce, the lowest since April 20, 1993.
Dealers said the metals were drifting lower as gold, the leader of the precious metals complex, had come under heavy selling pressure in recent days.
"There's nothing fundamental pushing platinum and palladium lower. They're just being sucked down by the bearish sentiment surrounding gold," a London-based dealer said.

Platinum, used by the auto industry for catalytic converters and in jewellery-making, has steadily edged lower in recent months due to ample supply in the market and insufficient demand to buoy the price.
Palladium, used primarily in electronics, catalysts and dentistry, was suffering from slack demand from chief importer Japan, dealers said.
